mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan Company Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization via Cross-Strait Mechanism: notarization by a Taiwan district court notary; authentication by the Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF); final verification by the Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS) or its designated sub-office on mainland China. No Hague Apostille is permissible because Taiwan is not a party to the Apostille Convention; the sequential SEF/ARATS route is mandatory and mutually exclusive with apostille.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act (公司法), Articles 1-10, 128-156, 154-388 (as amended)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commerce (商業司) or its regional offices
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Company Registration (公司登記申請書) and Articles of Incorporation (公司章程)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) in Taiwan; however, the capital must be sufficient to cover initial operating expenses and must be deposited into a temporary bank account in Taiwan. The deposit must be verified by a bank certificate and submitted with the incorporation application. The capital cannot be withdrawn until the company is registered and the bank account is activated.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED (the 'Company'), duly convened and held at [Registered Office], on [Date], at [Time]. Present: [Names of Directors]. The meeting was called to order by the Chairman, who confirmed that a quorum was present. After due deliberation, the following resolutions were unanimously adopted:

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: RESOLVED, that the Company's authorized share capital be set at [Amount] New Taiwan Dollars, divided into [Number] shares of par value [Amount] each, and that the initial paid-up capital be [Amount], to be subscribed by the sole shareholder, [Shareholder Name], in accordance with the Articles of Incorporation. The subscription shall be deposited into the Company's designated bank account, and the bank receipt shall be filed with the competent authority.

2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: RESOLVED, that the Company shall open a corporate bank account with [Bank Name], and that the Director, [Name], and the General Manager, [Name], are hereby authorized, jointly and severally, to sign all banking documents, including but not limited to account opening forms, deposit and withdrawal instructions, and loan agreements, on behalf of the Company.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company shall be located at [Full Address], and that the Company shall file the necessary notices with the Ministry of Economic Affairs to record such address as the official registered office.

4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed as the Chairman of the Board, [Name] as the General Manager, and [Name] as the Company Secretary, each to serve until the next annual general meeting or until their successors are appointed. The Chairman is authorized to represent the Company in all matters, the General Manager to manage day-to-day operations, and the Company Secretary to maintain corporate records and ensure statutory compliance.

5. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION: RESOLVED, that the officers of the Company are authorized to execute, file, and deliver all necessary documents with the Ministry of Economic Affairs, tax authorities, and other regulatory bodies, and to engage legal counsel and accountants as needed, to complete the incorporation process and to ensure ongoing compliance with all applicable laws.

All resolutions were passed unanimously. The meeting was adjourned.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commerce – Online Name Reservation System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application through the MOEA's online portal, providing the proposed company name in both Chinese and English, the intended business scope (online retail of oversized furniture and home decor), and the full details of the sole shareholder (the foreign parent company). The system will automatically check for conflicts with existing registered names and trademarks. Upon approval, a name reservation certificate is issued, valid for six months. This certificate must be attached to the subsequent incorporation application. Ensure that the name complies with Taiwan's naming guidelines, including the use of 'Limited' or 'Co., Ltd.' as a suffix.
required_dossiers: Shareholder identification documents (passport or corporate registration certificate)
Power of attorney if using an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to conflict or non-compliance, file a formal appeal with the MOEA within 15 days, providing evidence of distinctiveness or a revised name. Alternatively, submit a new application with a different name. The MOEA will reconsider the appeal within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Incorporation Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan Notary Public or District Court Notarization Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation, the shareholder resolution, and the board resolution (as per the pro-forma above). Have these documents notarized by a licensed notary public in Taiwan. Simultaneously, open a temporary bank account in the company's name and deposit the paid-up capital. Obtain a bank capital verification certificate confirming the deposit. Secure a lease agreement for the registered office address, which must be a physical location in Taiwan. All documents must be in Chinese or accompanied by a certified Chinese translation. The notarization process verifies the authenticity of signatures and the legality of the content.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of all directors and shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies deficiencies, correct the documents and resubmit for notarization. If the bank delays the capital verification, request a written explanation and escalate to the bank's compliance officer. Any corrections must be completed within 10 business days to avoid delays.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission to MOEA and Payment of Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Compile the complete incorporation application package, including the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the name reservation certificate, the bank capital verification certificate, the lease agreement, and the application form. Submit the package online via the MOEA's Company Registration System or in person at the MOEA office. Pay the registration fee (approximately USD 150) via the designated payment gateway. The MOEA will review the application for compliance with the Company Act. Upon approval, the MOEA issues the Company Registration Certificate, which is the official proof of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Identification of all directors and shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MOEA issues a query or suspension, respond to the specific deficiencies within 30 days. Provide additional documentation or clarifications as requested. If the application is deemed withdrawn due to non-response, re-submit the entire application with a new fee. The MOEA may also request an in-person interview if there are compliance concerns.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Registrations and Bank Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Finance (Taxation), Bureau of Labor, and Commercial Banks
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Company Registration Certificate, register for tax purposes with the National Taxation Bureau to obtain a Unified Business Number (UBIN). Register with the Bureau of Labor for labor insurance and health insurance for employees. Activate the temporary bank account by presenting the Company Registration Certificate, the board resolution authorizing the account, and the UBIN. The bank will convert the temporary account into a permanent corporate account. Additionally, register for any required business licenses (e.g., e-commerce platform registration if applicable) and file the initial tax declaration.
required_dossiers: Labor and health insurance registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is delayed, pay any applicable penalties and file the registration within the extended deadline. For labor registration, contact the Bureau of Labor to resolve any discrepancies. If the bank refuses to activate the account, provide additional corporate documents or obtain a legal opinion from a Taiwan attorney. All remedial actions must be completed within 15 business days to avoid operational disruptions.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China, acting through provincial and municipal tax services. The online electronic portal is the STA National Unified Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax), including the export tax refund module.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the PRC WFOE: (1) obtain establishment registration from the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and receive the business license showing the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which is the mandatory Chinese Tax Identification Number; (2) within 30 days after issuance of the business license, complete tax registration through the local STA tax service office or the Electronic Tax Bureau platform, linking the USCC to Corporate Income Tax, VAT, stamp tax, and withholding obligations; (3) if annual taxable VAT sales exceed RMB 5,000,000, apply for mandatory general VAT taxpayer status, or elect general taxpayer status voluntarily when eligible; (4) apply for the electronic tax certificate and digital certificate needed to access e-Tax, issue invoices, and file export tax refund declarations; (5) for the non-resident Taiwan parent or other foreign non-resident entity without a Chinese permanent establishment, a separate Chinese TIN is not required unless the entity derives China-source income; in that case, non-resident tax registration and withholding registration must be completed with the STA branch administering the payer or the income source.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The WFOE is a PRC resident enterprise subject to Corporate Income Tax on worldwide income, is not a pass-through entity, and is not located in a tax-exempt zone. Non-resident shareholders remain subject to PRC dividend withholding tax on distributions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The PRC does not provide a check-the-box election or hybrid mismatch election for entity classification. The only available tax-status election under PRC law is the VAT classification election between small-scale taxpayer and general VAT taxpayer, which does not alter entity-level income tax treatment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Law of the People's Republic of China, the VAT implementing regulations, and the export tax rebate (exemption) measures.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: VAT registration is mandatory for all newly formed WFOEs from the date of establishment; no monetary exemption applies. Compulsory general VAT taxpayer registration is triggered when annual taxable sales exceed RMB 5,000,000. Below the threshold, the entity may remain a small-scale taxpayer using the simplified VAT collection method.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: VAT invoices must be issued through the STA-approved electronic invoice platform; the Golden Tax Phase IV system receives invoice data in near real time. Fully digitalized electronic invoices are recognized and carry a unique invoice number and an anti-counterfeit tax control code or QR code. General taxpayers may use API-based integration for ERP-to-tax-system transmission. Special VAT invoices used for input tax credit are verified in the national VAT invoice verification database. There is no separate physical fiscal stamp; the STA digital system performs anti-fraud validation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from China are eligible for VAT zero-rating and export tax refund only when (a) the goods are physically exported and released under a PRC Customs export declaration; (b) the exporter is the PRC WFOE and holds general VAT taxpayer status with corresponding VAT special invoices for purchases; (c) export proceeds are repatriated in accordance with State Administration of Foreign Exchange rules; and (d) the goods are not on the prohibited-export list. Cross-border e-commerce export modes recognized by customs are available for oversized home-furniture shipments, including direct B2C, B2B, and overseas-warehouse modes, and may use simplified export clearance and refund procedures. Offshore digital services are not part of this goods-based entity; China applies separate rules to qualifying cross-border digital services.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (official PRC export goods customs declaration record)
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or international logistics proof of export shipment
Commercial Invoice and Packing List for the exported furniture
Export sales contract or purchase order, if required for customs valuation
Bank receipt or foreign exchange settlement record evidencing repatriation of export proceeds
Export tax-refund declaration data filed through the STA Electronic Tax Bureau export tax refund module
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA, with General Administration of Customs data, automatically cross-checks export declarations, logistics, VAT invoices, and foreign exchange receipts. If a zero-rating or export tax refund claim is fraudulent or lacks substantiation, the tax authority must recover the refunded amount, impose a late-payment surcharge, and levy a penalty of 50% to 500% of the tax evaded under the PRC Tax Collection Administration Law. Serious cases constitute criminal tax fraud and may lead to criminal liability, suspension or revocation of export tax refund qualifications, and extended retrospective clawback generally up to five years for fraudulent acts.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) as the central bank, acting through the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) as the delegated foreign-exchange administration; the Taiwan-side outward remittance approval is governed by the Central Bank of Taiwan (CBC).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The RMB is conditionally convertible under China's managed floating exchange-rate regime. Current-account transactions, including e-commerce sale of furniture, freight, warehousing, platform fees, and ordinary trade payments, are generally freely convertible; the bank must still perform a veracity check against the commercial contract, invoice, customs declaration, and logistics evidence. Capital-account transactions remain under strict SAFE control. An inbound equity investment from Taiwan must first complete the FDI foreign exchange registration; the contribution is then received into a foreign exchange capital account and can be settled into RMB under the corporate negative-list rules for permitted working-capital expenditures. Profit remittance to the Taiwan parent is lawful only after the WFOE's annual corporate income tax settlement, based on an audited distributable profit amount, with proof of withholding tax and no past-due SAFE reporting. Repatriation of registered capital beyond accumulated profits requires capital reduction, deregistration, and prior SAFE approval. Surplus funds cannot be used for speculative cross-border transfers. All FX flows must be supported by underlying business truthfulness; a bank that detects documentation mismatches will freeze the payment and report to SAFE. Therefore, treasury planning must separate current-account receipts, capital-account injections, and dividend outflows into distinct audit trails.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: China has abolished the historical forced surrender ratio for export goods in foreign currency. The WFOE may keep USD or RMB export proceeds in a current-account foreign exchange account or convert the entire amount into RMB at the onshore spot rate; no minimum conversion percentage is mandated. The statutory discipline is receipt matching and reporting: if the export proceeds do not arrive within 90 days from the customs export date, the enterprise must file a deferred-collection trade credit report with SAFE, usually by the 30th day after the 90-day threshold. If the delay exceeds 180 days, the bank will treat the transaction as a high-risk anomaly and may require item-by-item proof of collection schedule. For cross-border e-commerce, the WFOE must reconcile platform settlements with customs e-commerce lists and cannot leave export receipts offshore without SAFE approval.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech EMIs are not legally viable as a primary treasury channel for a PRC WFOE. Offshore digital banks and electronic money institutions such as Wise, Revolut Business, Payoneer, and Airwallex do not hold Chinese banking licenses and cannot open onshore corporate settlement accounts, hold client RMB deposits, or perform capital account verification in China. PBOC and SAFE restrict corporate account takeover and client fund custody to licensed Chinese commercial banks and qualified clearing institutions. A small number of licensed cross-border payment institutions may handle export collection for e-commerce, but they are sub-channels and cannot substitute for the Tier-1 domestic bank account required for statutory capital, tax payment, payroll, and profit repatriation. Therefore, the blueprint should use Tier-1 Chinese banks as the primary rail and integrate fintech platforms only as downstream collection and card-settlement tools.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A WFOE opening a corporate account in China generally requires the legal representative to appear physically in the designated bank branch with the original business license, unified social credit certificate, article of association, company chop set (company, finance, and legal-representative chops), and valid identity documents. For a Taiwan-resident legal representative, an in-person visit is strongly preferred. Some Tier-1 banks permit video-verified KYC for a non-mainland legal representative if a local authorized agent with a notarized and authenticated power of attorney appears at the branch and the Taiwan-issued identity documents are notarially authenticated; however, the ultimate decision remains with the bank's compliance committee. Statutory directors not acting as legal representatives or signatories normally do not need to appear unless they appear on the beneficial ownership chain above a control threshold.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity through a Taiwan corporate shareholder with a cross-strait chain that could conceal a nominee or shell arrangement
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized Taiwan company registration extract and certificate of incorporation; board resolution of the Taiwan parent approving the WFOE capital injection; group structure chart signed by the UBO; UBO passport or Taiwan ID, proof of residential address, and tax identification; audited accounts of the Taiwan parent for the last two years; bank statement evidencing the source of the remitted funds; KYC declaration that no third-party nominee or shell is used.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Fragmented, small-ticket, multi-currency settlements from Stripe and Affirm BNPL platforms that obscure revenue ownership and may commingle unrelated customer funds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve months of original platform settlement reports from Stripe and Affirm; item-level reconciliation by order, refund, chargeback, and payout currency; platform merchant identification credentials; API export of transaction IDs; logistics manifests and customs e-commerce export declarations matching the revenue; payment-flow narrative confirming no use of third-party collection accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large lump-sum inbound registered capital from Taiwan into a newly-established WFOE with no operating history, suggesting possible round-tripping or conduit financing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE FDI registration certificate and bank reference number; Taiwan parent bank statements showing the exact withdrawal; audited financial statements and tax clearance certificate of the Taiwan parent; board resolution and capital contribution schedule; use-of-proceeds business plan; written confirmation that funds do not originate from borrowed funds or offshore financiers; loyalty of the injection to the registered capital amount in the Articles.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Oversized furniture e-commerce may be used as a vehicle for sanctions evasion, diversion to embargoed destinations, or under-invoicing of high-value ship-borne cargo
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Harmonized System classification certificate (HS 9403); export sales invoices; complete set of bills of lading or air waybills; recipient and storage-address KYC for trade counterparties; sanctions and denied-party screening report; export-control self-assessment confirming no restricted end-use; customs export declarations; warranty letter from purchasers that goods are not for military or embargoed end users.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Taiwan parent must first obtain the outward remittance approval or facility headroom required by the Central Bank of Taiwan, then transmit USD or RMB via SWIFT MT103 directly to the WFOE's foreign exchange capital account at a Chinese Tier-1 bank. The bank will verify the SAFE FDI registration code and match the remittance amount against the approved registered capital. The Field 70 remittance information should carry the SAFE registration number and the China BOP purpose code for inbound direct investment equity injection. After receipt, the bank performs capital-account income verification and may allow the funds to be converted to RMB on a willing-settlement basis for permitted operating expenditures. If the local administration for market regulation or the bank's internal policy requests an accounting confirmation, a certified public accountant capital verification report or a funds-in statement audited by a licensed CPA must be added before excepted payments.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For domestic supplier and freight payments, the WFOE should use RMB transfers through the Chinese national payment clearing system. For cross-border payments to foreign factories, carriers, or overseas warehouses, permitted rails include SWIFT MT103 for direct payment of confirmed invoices, commercial letters of credit (sight or usance) for large-container furniture purchases, and documentary collections (D/P or D/A) for moderate-risk counterparties. The bank will require the underlying trade contract, pro-forma or commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading, customs declaration, and if applicable the insurance certificate before booking the FX. The WFOE must not use trade channels to pre-pay unrelated expenses or to square intercompany balances that lack a genuine business purpose.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/RMB foreign-exchange forward contracts covering trade-related and direct-investment-related cash flows, with tenors generally up to 12 months and real-demand documentation submitted to the designated onshore bank
USD/RMB foreign-exchange swaps for short-term conversion and re-conversion of commercially justified currency mismatches

Plain-vanilla USD/RMB foreign-exchange options (call/put with premium) permitted under SAFE real-need rules; offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) cannot be booked by a PRC WFOE without specific SAFE approval

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ultimate beneficial owner register confirmation and statutory register audit cover note
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of directors and company secretary; made available to Ministry of Economic Affairs and Financial Supervisory Commission examiners upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually before the shareholders' meeting and within 30 days after any shareholding transfer or UBO change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain or update the statutory register books can result in fines against the responsible officer, adverse findings in regulator examinations, and in severe cases a compulsory strike-off of the company registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements, annual business report, and profit distribution resolution approved by shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Taiwan company shareholders' meeting; then filed with the Ministry of Economic Affairs (Department of Commercial and Industrial Registration) where statutory thresholds apply
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after fiscal year-end; a calendar-year WFOE must conclude the meeting by 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Responsible persons may be fined NT$20,000 to NT$200,000 for failure to hold the annual meeting; continued non-compliance may cause the competent authority to order a meeting or apply for compulsory dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Certified independent auditor's report and audited financial statements (for mandatory-audit companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial and Industrial Registration; feasibility copies to the local National Taxation Bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audited statements must be approved with the annual financial statements by 30 June and filed with the MOEA within 15 days after shareholder approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to deliver audited statements or to file required records may impose administrative fines of NT$10,000 to NT$50,000 per item on responsible officers and, if persistent, support cancellation of relevant tax or trade licenses and strike-off action.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax return and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Finance, National Taxation Bureau (local jurisdiction office for the WFOE registered address)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year taxpayer, file between 1 May and 31 May of the following year; fiscal-year taxpayers file within five months after year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment adds a 1% monthly surcharge on unpaid tax up to 10%; late filing brings fixed fines plus interest at the one-year time-deposit rate; underpayment penalties can reach three times the understated amount; severe default triggers tax liens, asset seizure, and tax registration strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Bi-monthly value-added and business tax return (sales and purchase declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Finance, National Taxation Bureau (local jurisdiction office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six returns per year, due by the 15th day of the month following each two-month period; for the January-February period the return is due 15 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late return or under-declaration results in fixed penalties up to NT$15,000 plus late-payment surcharge on unpaid VAT; repeated failures can lead to tax assessment, asset seizure, and deregistration for business tax purposes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual foreign investor operation and investment status report (foreign-owned company compliance filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of the foreign-invested company's fiscal year; a calendar-year WFOE files by 30 June unless an extension is granted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted filing may block future investment applications, restrict dividend and profit repatriation through the foreign-exchange approval process, and ultimately lead to withdrawal or cancellation of the foreign investment approval.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: In Taiwan the decisive quantitative trigger is balance-sheet size, not turnover or headcount: any non-public company with paid-in capital exceeding NT$30 million must be independently audited by a certified public accountant; public issuers and companies regulated under the Securities and Exchange Act must always be audited; banks, financial holding companies, insurance, securities and futures enterprises must be audited under their sectoral laws; supervised license-holders may be separately obligated by their license. For the target WFOE, headcount and revenue do not create the audit obligation, but an audited set of financial statements is required if the WFOE's paid-in capital exceeds the NT$30 million threshold or if the Investment Commission or financing counterparties contractually require certification.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Public companies and financial institutions apply IFRS as endorsed by the Financial Supervisory Commission; non-public companies may apply Taiwan IFRS, Taiwan SME Financial Reporting Standards, or local GAAP consistently; all statutory accounts must also comply with the Business Entity Accounting Act and the Regulations on Uniform Accounting System. The WFOE should adopt IFRS or SME-IFRS for the e-commerce sales revenue recognition of oversized furniture transactions.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The WFOE must maintain, at the registered office in Taiwan, a complete set of statutory books, including shareholder and director registers, meeting minutes, and charges or security registrations. Any transfer of shares that changes record ownership must be posted to the share register and to the MOEA registration within 30 days of the transfer; a change in foreign-investor status must also be reported to the Investment Commission in the same event-driven 30-day window. Before the annual shareholders' meeting, the board must confirm the ultimate beneficial owner schedule and update the UBO records for any material changes, thereby satisfying the annual confirmation and the 30-day reporting discipline.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - USD 2,500 per year for a Taiwanese registered office and licensed corporate secretarial agent
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - USD 15,000 per year for an e-commerce WFOE requiring IFRS/SME-IFRS audited financial statements and revenue-recognition audit procedures

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard 25% CIT rate for resident enterprises. Small and low-profit enterprises with annual taxable income not exceeding RMB 3 million enjoy a preferential effective 5% rate (25% of taxable income applied at the 20% statutory rate). Qualified High and New Technology Enterprises use 15%. Qualifying R&D expenses receive an additional 100% super-deduction. A 15% preferential rate applies to certain encouraged industries in Western China. No general patent box regime applies; free-trade-zone incentives are mainly non-CIT cash awards, customs and VAT preferences, not blanket CIT holidays. Loss carryforward is generally 5 years; high-tech and small low-profit enterprises may carry losses forward 10 years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form A100000 Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return (Main Form), with supporting schedules A105000 (tax adjustments), A105080 (depreciation), A108000 (foreign tax credit) and G100000 (related-party transaction reporting), filed through the State Taxation Administration electronic tax filing portal (e-tax portal).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with quarterly provisional prepayment returns using Form A200000 filed within 15 days after each quarter-end.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual CIT return must be filed within 5 months after fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year taxpayer, the deadline is 31 May of the following year. Quarterly prepayment returns are due within 15 days after the end of each quarter.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from online retail sales of oversized furniture, home decor, delivery surcharges and installation service income, net of returns, allowances and commercial discounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All revenue earned by the China WFOE is subject to CIT on a worldwide basis. Recognize revenue regardless of payment rail, including Stripe and Affirm BNPL settlement. Cross-border sales to Taiwan-related distributors or online marketplace operators must be made at arm's length; unsupported under-pricing will be adjusted under CIT Law Articles 41, 44 and 48.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold, including inventory purchases, inbound freight, warehouse costs, import duties and direct overhead for the oversized furniture products.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If inventory is purchased from a Taiwan-related party, use the customs invoice and transfer pricing study to support the price. Related-party material purchases exceeding statutory thresholds require contemporaneous Local File documentation. Expenses attributable to related-party imports that are not borne at arm's length are disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 / Line 3 - Business taxes and surcharges
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible enterprise tax and surcharge items, including city maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges, local education surcharges, stamp duty, property tax, vehicle tax and land use tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: VAT itself is not a deductible expense. Withholding income tax paid on dividends, interest or royalties to the Taiwan shareholder is also not deductible. Any tax holder or surcharge withheld from a non-resident supplier must be evidenced by tax payment receipts and correctly classified.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Marketing and advertising, platform commissions, payment processing fees, oversized-freight logistics, after-sales warranty, online marketplace fees and related selling overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border service fees paid to a Taiwan affiliate for marketing, IT, or customer service must satisfy the beneficial service test and arm's-length charge. Imported services may trigger 6% VAT and non-resident withholding tax; if the Taiwan affiliate performs no substantive function, the expense is disallowed and treaty benefits may be denied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 / Line 5 - General and administrative expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Management salaries, office rent, legal, audit, bookkeeping, insurance, security and general corporate expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees charged by the Taiwan parent or affiliates for pure stewardship or duplicate activities are not deductible. A specific service agreement, actual work records, cost allocation breakdown and an arm's-length markup are required. Payments to the Taiwan related party must be supported by contemporaneous service documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest expense on loans, bank fees, guarantee fees, foreign exchange losses and other financing expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest on shareholder loans is restricted by the thin-capitalization rule: debt-to-equity ratio for a non-financial enterprise is 2:1. The interest rate must be at arm's length. Interest paid to a Taiwan non-resident beneficial owner is subject to 10% statutory WHT, reduced to 7% under the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement only if the Taiwan lender has a valid tax residency certificate and beneficial ownership.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit before tax computed as operating revenue minus operating cost, taxes, selling, administrative and financial expenses, plus other gains and losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Tax losses may be carried forward 5 years (10 for qualifying small low-profit or high-tech enterprises). If the WFOE has loss carryforwards arising from related-party restructuring, the tax authorities may deny the loss unless the restructuring has legitimate commercial substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 / Line 14 - Taxable income after adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after adding back non-deductible expenses, applying tax adjustments, deducting tax-exempt income, and offsetting allowable losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All related-party transactions with Taiwan affiliates must be reported on Schedule G100000. The taxpayer must maintain the Local File, Master File and County-by-Country Report when thresholds are met. Treaty benefits for foreign tax credits and reduced withholding rates are substantiated outside the main return but must be reconciled with the taxable-income adjustments.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual CIT return attracts late-filing penalty under the Tax Collection and Administration Law: RMB 2,000 for ordinary late filing and RMB 10,000 for serious cases. Late payment accrues a daily 0.05% surcharge on the unpaid tax. Understatement due to falsified invoices, hidden revenue or related-party manipulation triggers a 50% to 500% penalty on the underpaid tax under TCAL Article 63. Criminal tax evasion under Criminal Law Article 201 can lead to imprisonment up to 3 years for lesser amounts and up to 7 years for enormous amounts, plus criminal fines, major-tax-violation blacklisting and exit/travel bans for the responsible directors.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory withholding tax on gross dividends paid by a China resident enterprise to a non-resident enterprise shareholder. Under the Cross-Strait Agreement on Avoidance of Double Taxation on Income, the rate is reduced to 5% if the Taiwan beneficial owner is a resident of Taiwan and holds directly not less than 25% of the paid-up capital of the WFOE; otherwise 10% remains applicable.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the Taiwan shareholder must obtain a Taiwan Tax Residency Certificate issued by the Taiwan competent tax authority for the relevant calendar year and deliver it to the WFOE before the dividend payment date. The Taiwan shareholder must also execute a Beneficial Ownership declaration and maintain evidence of substantive business activities in Taiwan, including local premises, employees, bank accounts, board minutes, risk-taking and decision-making. The WFOE as withholding agent must file the non-resident withholding tax return through the e-tax portal, attach the TRC, the 25% shareholding record and a board resolution authorizing the treaty-rate application. The local tax bureau may require the agreement, invoices or contracts, and audited financial statements to prove no conduit arrangement. If the treaty application is rejected, the difference between 5% and 10% becomes immediately payable with late-payment interest and possible penalties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory interest withholding is 10% CIT WHT on gross interest paid to non-resident enterprises; under the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement the rate is 7% for interest paid to a Taiwan resident beneficial owner. Royalties paid to a Taiwan non-resident are subject to 10% CIT WHT domestically and 7% under the Cross-Strait Agreement if the Taiwan beneficial owner has substance and is not a conduit. Royalties also carry 6% VAT plus local surcharges on the VAT, which are not reduced by the tax arrangement. Excessive interest within the 7% treaty rate may still be disallowed if thin-capitalization or transfer-pricing rules apply.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Contemporaneous Local File documentation is required under SAT Announcement 2016 No. 42 when annual related-party transactions exceed RMB 200 million for tangible assets, RMB 100 million for intangible assets, RMB 100 million for financial asset transactions, or RMB 40 million for provision or receipt of services. The Master File is required when the multinational group had consolidated revenue in the preceding year of at least RMB 5.5 billion and the enterprise engaged in related-party transactions. The Country-by-Country Report is required at the same RMB 5.5 billion group revenue threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China applies the substance-over-form doctrine and the general anti-avoidance rule under CIT Law Article 47. For Cross-Strait treaty benefits, the Taiwan shareholder must be the beneficial owner and must not be a shell or conduit. The economic substance analysis tests whether the Taiwan entity performs core income-generating activities, has real employees, premises, decision-making authority, asset ownership and risk assumption. Formal registration alone is insufficient; a paper entity used only to access the 5% dividend or 7% royalty rate will be disregarded and full domestic withholding will be applied with penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion via Transfer Pricing Manipulation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE sells oversized home furniture to a Taiwan-related distributor at a below-arm's-length price, or purchases furniture and logistics services from a Taiwan affiliate at an inflated price, while the Taiwan affiliate performs no substantive distribution, inventory risk or service functions, and the WFOE fails to prepare a Local File, Master File or contemporaneous transfer pricing study.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CIT Law Articles 41, 44, 47 and 48; Tax Collection and Administration Law Articles 35 and 63. Tax authorities can reassess income by arm's-length pricing, add 0.05% daily late-payment interest, and impose a penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid CIT. Where the evasion exceeds the criminal threshold, Criminal Law Article 201 imposes criminal fines and imprisonment up to 7 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed false transfer pricing contracts or caused the understatement of income may have the corporate veil pierced under PRC Company Law Article 20; they can be jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax and restitution. Criminal responsibility attaches to the persons who organized and directed the evasion, which can include imprisonment and criminal fines. The director may be placed on the major tax violation blacklist, triggering travel bans, exit restrictions and denial of government procurement or banking facilities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Violation on Profit Repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE distributes dividends to the Taiwan corporate shareholder and wires the gross amount abroad without withholding 10% non-resident enterprise income tax, or without completing the Cross-Strait treaty relief procedure to claim 5%, including obtaining the Taiwan Tax Residency Certificate and Beneficial Ownership substantiation before the payment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CIT Law Articles 37 and 40; TCAL Article 69. The withholding agent is liable for the undeclared withholding tax and subject to a penalty of 50% to 300% of the tax that should have been withheld. TCAL Article 62 additionally allows a penalty up to RMB 10,000 for failure to file the withholding return. The tax authority may also collect the unpaid tax directly from the Taiwan shareholder beneficiary.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who knowingly approved a dividend declaration without legal retained earnings or without withholding and remitting the WHT may be personally liable to compensate the company for losses under PRC Company Law Article 149. Where company assets are diverted abroad leaving creditors unpaid, courts may pierce the limited-liability veil and impose personal asset restitution. Serious failures involving concealment of taxable income are criminal tax evasion under Criminal Law Article 201; the responsible director faces imprisonment up to 7 years, criminal fines, blacklisting and exit bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Treaty Abuse and Shell Company Arrangement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Taiwan shareholder is a newly formed shell entity with no substantive employees, premises, bank accounts, business contracts or decision-making, created solely to receive royalties or dividends from the WFOE at the reduced Cross-Strait tax rates; the WFOE pays inflated royalties or management fees to the shell to drain Chinese profits, and the shell lacks economic substance and beneficial ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CIT Law Article 47 and SAT Announcement 2018 No. 5. Treaty benefits are denied, the shell is disregarded, and the income is recharacterized as taxable to the China WFOE or otherwise subject to full 10% WHT, plus late-payment interest and a 50% to 500% evasion penalty. If the royalty payments are supported by fraudulent invoices, Criminal Law Article 205 on false invoicing may apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who created and operated the sham structure can be criminally liable for organizing tax evasion under Criminal Law Article 201, with imprisonment up to 7 years and fines. Civilly, the corporate veil is pierceable because the shell is used to abuse legal form; directors may be ordered to return misappropriated royalty or dividend monies from personal assets. The responsible directors may be blacklisted as major non-compliant taxpayers, effectively barring cross-border travel and freezing bank accounts until the tax liability is settled.
